CVE-2026-102664.title: ProxySQL: Uninitialized heap read in MySQL compressed packet decompression via zlib path
CVE-2026-102664.description: ProxySQL is a proxy for MySQL and its forks, as well as PostgreSQL. Prior to 3.0.10, 3.1.10, and 4.0.10, decompress_mysql_payload() in lib/mysql_data_stream.cpp accepts a zlib stream when uncompress() returns Z_OK without checking that the actual output length equals the attacker-controlled payload_length. An authenticated MySQL client that negotiates compression can overstate payload_length, causing buffer2array() to parse the uninitialized tail of a heap buffer as MySQL packet headers and forward stale data to the backend. Backend error responses can disclose prior SQL queries, result data, credentials, or session state, and malformed lengths can also cause excessive allocations. This issue is fixed in versions 3.0.10, 3.1.10, and 4.0.10.

CVE-2026-92853.title: Out-of-bounds Read via a Zero-length TLS 1.3 Certificate Message in NetX Secure
CVE-2026-92853.description:
The TLS 1.3 Certificate-message parser in NetX Secure decrements the message length to skip a context byte without first establishing that the message has a byte to skip. A zero-length Certificate message therefore wraps the unsigned length to `0xFFFFFFFF`, which makes the bounds check that follows vacuous and sends the parser reading past the session packet buffer.

The trigger is a four-byte handshake header and requires no cryptographic validity. It is reachable pre-authentication.

CVE-2026-99034.title: mmc: sdhci-sprd: disable runtime PM on remove
CVE-2026-99034.description:
In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved:

mmc: sdhci-sprd: disable runtime PM on remove

sdhci_sprd_probe() enables runtime PM, while sdhci_sprd_remove() does
not perform the corresponding runtime PM cleanup.

The probe failure path disables runtime PM before disabling the clocks,
but the normal remove path directly disables clocks that are also
managed by the runtime PM callbacks. If the device is runtime
suspended, those clocks may already be disabled.

Resume the device before removal, disable runtime PM and drop the
temporary runtime PM reference before disabling the clocks.

This issue was found by manual code inspection.
